Complete stream acquisition bounds registry bytes, received artifact bytes and gzip expansion, covers stalled headers/bodies, cancels abandoned readers and shares the artifact deadline across acquisition and decompression. Public route identity and private ownership/projection requirements remain intact.

A newer selection cancels earlier work. Response observation captures no extra request and preserves the caller response; older headers/bodies cannot replace newer captures, and failure of the latest capture explicitly clears earlier evidence. Owner identity changes still invalidate capture.

limitations: Exact static deployment remains pending. This stage changes browser/build code only; no native engine deployment is required.

The authenticated private-artifacts adapter still buffers upstream bytes before returning a response to this reader. Its earlier buffer is a separately reproduced next task; this change does not claim to bound that adapter.

A synchronous parser cannot be preempted by browser timers; accepted bytes and nesting are bounded and artifact elapsed time is checked after parsing. Rendering allocation is not exhaustively bounded. Numbers retain JavaScript binary64 semantics, not arbitrary precision.

Original caller parsers remain separate from the strict inspector capture. No provider observation, normal private publication, point-in-time qualification, independent evidence, portfolio reconciliation or trading skill is established. All ten platform workstreams remain open.
